verdict.rationale: Loops ships its own CLI that installs non-interactively and supports JSON output for scripting, plus a REST API with Bearer-token auth, so headless automation is directly supported. The docs never explicitly cover CI pipelines or non-interactive CLI authentication, so coverage of the story is partial rather than complete. missing for 10: explicit CI/CD documentation (e.g. GitHub Actions examples), documented non-interactive or environment-variable auth for the CLI, independent or hands-on corroboration of CI use.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: All commands support JSON output (-o json) for scripting and multi-team auth (--team <name>) for switching between workspaces.
Manage contacts, send events, trigger transactional emails, and test your integration, all from the terminal.
Install the Loops CLI with curl, Homebrew, Windows PowerShell, or Go.
add an Authorization header and set the API key as a Bearer token
